resources.string: Playing the raw channel audio — check whether the frequency is in use before keying up.\nRADE speech is muted while monitoring; the sync indicator stays live. Tap again to return to RADE decode.
Speak into the mic, then tap TX to transmit.\nUse phone volume keys to adjust TX level — ALC should show minimal or no deflection.
Transmitting… Tap TX again to return to RX.\nALC should show minimal or no deflection — lower phone volume if ALC is moving.
Hold the TX button and speak; release to return to RX.\nUse phone volume keys to adjust TX level — ALC should show minimal or no deflection.
Transmitting… Release the button to return to RX.\nALC should show minimal or no deflection — lower phone volume if ALC is moving.
When on, the TX button works like a walkie-talkie: transmit only while the button is held, and return to RX the moment it is released. When off, tapping TX toggles between transmit and receive.
Choose the mic used when transmitting. A USB-hub external mic gives better audio and faster keying than the Bluetooth mic. (The Bluetooth mic option below overrides this when enabled.)

Boosts your voice into the RADE encoder. If other stations report low modulation, raise this while watching the TX level meter; lower it if your voice sounds distorted. (Digital Gain only affects RX.)

Captures TX voice from the Bluetooth headset mic. When an LE Audio (LC3) headset is available, RX/TX uses Android call-audio routing so the headset mic and speaker stay on LC3; otherwise TX may fall back to classic SCO. In this call-audio mode the headset firmware may disable its own noise cancelling, and loudness follows the call volume (the volume keys control it while running). Experimental. Off = phone mic.
Reporter is turned off — enable it in Settings → FreeDV Reporter.
Set your callsign in Settings → TX Callsign to start reporting.
e.g. portable from JO31, IC-7300 + dipole
Free-text shown next to your station on qso.freedv.org. Up to 80 characters. Remembered across restarts and re-pushed automatically after every reconnect; press Update to push the current text now.
Maidenhead locator (e.g. PM95). Required by qso.freedv.org — when empty, the app reports UN00KN (unknown location). Tap GPS to fill it from your position automatically.
Connect to qso.freedv.org to see active stations
This will permanently delete all reception logs. This cannot be undone.
Start receiving to create a session
Boost weak USB audio input. Adjust until peak level is around -15 to -5 dBFS.
Use wired audio when connected; otherwise use the phone speaker. Select Bluetooth explicitly to route playback there.
Let Android route playback, useful for USB DACs and external speakers.

Plays a 1 kHz tone to the selected output and shows where Android actually routed it — this tells a routing problem apart from \"no decoded speech yet\". Try it with USB audio both connected and disconnected.

Drive level of the RADE waveform into the rig\'s USB audio input. Too low → ALC barely moves, reduced TX power. Too high → ALC slams, distorted signal. Also check your rig\'s USB MOD Level (IC-7300: Menu → SET → Connectors → USB MOD Level).
Your callsign will be encoded in the EOO (End-of-Over) frame during TX.
Select the audio interface for RADE TX modulated output.
Hides the spectrum and waterfall and stops FFT processing to lighten the load on low-end devices, helping decoding run smoothly.

Switches TX and RX to the new RADE V2 waveform, just merged upstream and still being tested. V1 and V2 cannot hear each other on the air — both stations must use the same version. The end-of-over callsign is V1-only. Leave OFF for normal operation.
Capture the app\'s recent rig/CAT logs (rigctld, USB-serial bridge) to share when reporting a control problem. Reproduce the issue first, then capture and copy.
HF digital voice transceiver. Decodes and encodes RADE OFDM signals using on-device FARGAN neural vocoder.
This application is licensed under the GNU Lesser General Public License v2.1.

Select the SDR app serving CAT — the connection bridges through the bundled Hamlib. Thetis = TCP/IP CAT server, piHPSDR = RigCtl port (default 19090), Spark/Quisk = rigctld-protocol server (SparkSDR, Quisk). RADE audio still uses Android audio devices; OpenHPSDR I/Q streaming is not used.

Connect to the IC-705 over Wi-Fi using its built-in server. On the radio: Set ▸ Network ▸ Network Control = ON, and set a Network User name/password. Enter the radio\'s IP address. Control and audio both run over Wi-Fi — no USB cable needed.

150 ms suits Wi-Fi/LAN. Over LTE or a VPN choose 500–800 ms: the radio buffers this much TX audio, so late or lost packets no longer interrupt the transmitted signal and lost packets have time to be resent. PTT is held for the same time after the over so the callsign is not cut off. Applies on the next connect.

Direct openHPSDR (protocol 1) control of a Hermes-Lite 2 on your LAN: discovery, frequency, PTT and the I/Q stream all ride UDP port 1024 — no PC needed. Leave Host empty to auto-discover by broadcast. SSB (de)modulation is done in the app.
On = power amplifier + main antenna jack. Off = low-power (~10 mW) jack; the antenna jack stays on receive.
Adaptive predistortion that auto-corrects TX distortion (the same WDSP engine as Thetis). Effective with the PA on.

RX/TX audio rides Wi-Fi to Voicemeeter on your PC (VBAN protocol) whose virtual cables are the SDR\'s VAC — PureSignal etc. keep working, no sound card or cables between phone and PC. Set a Voicemeeter OUTGOING stream (48 kHz, PCM16) to this phone\'s IP, and select incoming stream "RADE-TX" for the TX direction. CAT port = the SDR\'s CAT server (blank/0 = no CAT, use VOX).
DTR/RTS modem lines. Turn off RTS if your USB-serial cable wires it to PTT.

For CAT-less interfaces that key the rig with the RTS line: pressing TX asserts RTS automatically and releases it after the over (after the callsign has played out). Leave the RTS switch above OFF when using this.
No rig connected: Set keeps this as your manual frequency and reports it to FreeDV Reporter.
RADE Decode needs to run in the background to continuously receive and decode signals. Some devices restrict background activity which may interrupt decoding.
Battery optimization is enabled — may interrupt decoding

Disabling battery optimization will increase power consumption while RADE Decode is running. The app only uses significant power when actively decoding (Start is pressed). You can re-enable optimization anytime in system settings.
Ensure \"Allow background activity\" is enabled in App Settings → Battery.
If using \"Battery Saver\" mode, add RADE Decode to the exception list.
Samsung: Settings → Battery → Background usage limits → Never sleeping apps → Add RADE Decode.
Samsung: Disable \"Adaptive battery\" or add app to \"Unmonitored apps\".
Samsung: Settings → Apps → RADE Decode → Battery → Unrestricted.
Xiaomi/POCO: Settings → Apps → RADE Decode → Battery saver → No restrictions.
Xiaomi/POCO: Settings → Battery → App battery saver → RADE Decode → No restrictions.
Xiaomi/POCO: Security app → Battery → App battery saver → RADE Decode → No restrictions.
Xiaomi/POCO: Enable \"Autostart\" for RADE Decode in Security settings.
Huawei/Honor: Settings → Battery → App launch → RADE Decode → Set to \"Manage manually\" and enable all toggles.
Huawei/Honor: Settings → Apps → RADE Decode → Battery → Enable \"Run in background\".
Huawei/Honor: Disable \"Power-intensive prompt\" for this app.
OPPO/Realme/OnePlus: Settings → Battery → More settings → Optimize battery use → RADE Decode → Don\'t optimize.
OnePlus: Settings → Battery → Battery optimization → RADE Decode → Don\'t optimize.
OPPO/Realme: Enable \"Allow auto-launch\" and \"Allow background activity\".
vivo/iQOO: Settings → Battery → Background power consumption management → RADE Decode → Allow.
vivo/iQOO: i Manager → App manager → Autostart manager → Enable RADE Decode.
ASUS: Settings → Battery → PowerMaster → Auto-start manager → Enable RADE Decode.
Sony: Settings → Battery → Adaptive battery → Exceptions → Add RADE Decode.
Audio processing active — device rejected Unprocessed preset. Decoding may fail. Try a USB audio input.

USB/speaker TX also follows Android media volume. If power is low, adjust this and TX level gradually while checking the rig’s ALC. TX Mic Gain changes speech loudness, not RF drive. Network TX uses the radio/network drive settings instead.
PTT release not confirmed — retrying automatically. Check the radio; press Stop to retry now.
